content.title: NYT Connections hints today for #1,030: Clues and answers for Monday, April 6
content.text: Have you played today's New York Times Connections word game? This one was really tough to figure out, so I'll share some hints (and spoilers if you want them) to help you get through Monday's puzzle: #1,030. Don't feel bad for taking a peek — these puzzles are designed to confuse you.Since we're in this together, I'll share how I did each day. I made one mistake while solving the yellow group. Here's the order I solved all the groups in: yellow, green, blue, purple.If you're new to NYT Connections, we've got some tips to help you along the way. Also, check out today's Wordle hints and answer, as well as today’s Strands hints and answers.What is Connections?Connections is a surprisingly difficult word game created by the New York Times staff, and if you play, you're now considered a "connector." The goal is to figure out the theme of all four groups and four words per group that have something in common.How to play NYT ConnectionsUpon opening Connections, it may look confusing. There are 16 words presented in a four-by-four grid and your goal is to match four words into their respective color-coded groups (yellow, green, blue, purple). Yellow is the easiest to guess while purple is the hardest.Your job is to find out how the four words are connected to a specific group — there's always a theme. For instance, in one recent puzzle, the blue group hint was "related to buying a home" and the words were appraisal, escrow, insurance and mortgage.If you make a mistake when you submit, that's okay. You get four guesses before the game is over and the answers are revealed. You can also click on the lightbulb icon in the game to get some hints, but we'll also provide those here.If you find yourself obsessed with this game after completing just one puzzle, I've got bad news for you. You can only play once a day. The timer resets each night at midnight.Tips for playing NYT ConnectionsI only recently started playing Connections, but here are some tips I've found useful along the way.1. When you get an answer wrong, pay attention to the text that appears at the top of the puzzle. "One away" means you only got one word wrong. Analyze each word to find one that might fit better in another group and try a new word.2. If you're stuck, shuffle the board. You can shuffle as many times as you'd like to help you see some different word combinations.3. Try to find the easy yellow group words first. Those words usually stick out because they have so much in common — they're often synonyms of one another. But be wary of the trick words that could fit into multiple categories.4. Stumped? Come back to the puzzle later with a fresher mind. Trying to solve a difficult puzzle without "sleeping" on it might result in too many mistakes.Today's NYT Connections hintsCheck out these hints if you're having a hard time grouping them together.I'll give you my own hints:Yellow group: Where you'd go to danceGreen group: An investmentBlue group: A game you play where you hit a fake animal into a holePurple group: Shows where people singHere's one word from each group:Yellow group hint word: HoedownGreen group hint word: StakeBlue group hint word: MalletPurple group hint word: CarouserOkay, on to the official group names for a bigger hint.
